name: Tavira
title: Holidays in Tavira
intro: The Algarve's prettiest town, with a Roman bridge, a riverside of old houses and island beaches reached by little ferry. Here's what Tavira is like, when to go and how long to stay.
image_alt: A fishing boat on the river in Tavira, with the town's white houses behind
facts_note: The EU is bringing in new entry checks, so check the rules on GOV.UK before you book.
when_to_go: May, June, September and October are ideal, warm and sunny with quieter island beaches. July and August are hot and busy. Winter is mild and sunny, around 17°C, and the town stays lively.

things.name: Ilha de Tavira
things.blurb: A long sandy island beach, reached by a short ferry from town.

things.name: Praia do Barril
things.blurb: Walk or take a little train to the beach, past an anchor cemetery.

things.name: Roman bridge
things.blurb: The old bridge over the Gilão river, at the heart of town.

things.name: Castle and churches
things.blurb: Climb up to the castle garden for views over the rooftops.

things.name: Ria Formosa
things.blurb: Boat trips through a lagoon full of birds, including flamingos.

things.name: Cacela Velha
things.blurb: A tiny clifftop village above a lagoon beach, 15 minutes away.

faqs.question: Is Tavira worth visiting?
faqs.answer: Yes. It's one of the Algarve's most charming towns, with great island beaches and none of the high-rise resorts.

faqs.question: How do you get to Tavira?
faqs.answer: Fly into Faro, which has many direct flights from the UK, then take the train or drive, about 35 minutes.

faqs.question: What is the best time to visit Tavira?
faqs.answer: May, June, September and October, around 22 to 28°C.

faqs.question: Is the sea warmer in Tavira than the western Algarve?
faqs.answer: Yes. The eastern Algarve is calmer and a few degrees warmer, which suits families.

faqs.question: How many nights do you need in Tavira?
faqs.answer: A week gives time for the islands, the lagoon and a few day trips.
